author: Astrokillah
text:
I am going to stop trading for a while until I can figure out how to
draw FL correctly and use FL to plan my trade. I am going to use the
following rules of drawing FL, i.e. combining the classical RTM
definition and also what's proposed by Salivan.

The classical definition calls for a TG to be hit before we can draw FL,
 however, at times, there is no TG in sight, that's when Salivan's
definition comes in handy. I will also include DP in my chart, because
at this moment, I have not been able to figure out how to use FL to
explain all the price movement, so if someone could point to me how to
do without DP, I would be extremely grateful.

First up is the EURCAD chart, the objective is to draw FLs from Monthly
down to H1 so I can use the charts to plan a trade. I start with an
FXTOP chart from 1953 to 1986:

Point 1: Price established a range between the two outer green horizontal lines

Point 2: The upper horizontal line was engulfed, so a signal from ITs that they want price higher.

Point 3: Deepest retracement. I can't really see why price turned at
point 3, not at this scale. I was hoping that price bounced from FL-A,
so I could explain the bounce using the concept of FL but unfortunately
this didn't happen.

Point 4: Price got near the upper limit of broken range, flagged, and
then rallied strongly, making ATH (All Time High). I drew a rectangle
-B, is this a DP or a FL? By definition, B looked more like a DP. It is
not easy for price to make ATH, so B has to be a very strong and
important level. After price left Point 4, we could draw an FL from
Point 2 to Point 3 (orange rectangle), but this is a huge FL, it's
probably too big to be useful?

Point 5: Price returned to B and bounced.

Point 6: Price engulfed previous high, so RTM theory says, if price ever
 return to B again, that will be a safe location to go long.

Point 7: RTM theory is proven right, B indeed held and turned price again.

Point 8: Price broke ATH again, I drew rectangle C around a big kink,
but because it has not held price, according to our definition, this is
an FTR.

Point 9: Another 'kink was created, and it held price, so D is an FL

Point 10: E is a DP that engulfed FL-D

Point 11: F is an FL that engulfed FL-C

Point 12: G is an FL that engulfed B

Point 13: H is an FL that engulfed A.

That's all I have until 1986, there are lots of small kinks, but they
didn't seem to have broken any important levels on this time scale, so I
 don't know what to make of them.

Any feedback/correction, is greatly appreciated.

AK

author: staurum
text:
Hi AK,

Please bear in mind that when i made that post i had a less
understanding about flag limits then than i do now. However, the answers
 to your confusion are also in that post and Salivan's answer. Master
Sali answered it perfectly. It is right there in front of us, to be
honest.

"....So to him, FL = FTR that held price up. He didn't mention about the need to hit a TG...."

Not mentioning about the need to hit a TG does not mean there is no need
 to hit TG, so you gotta be careful with your logic deduction. I've read
 a few recent posts of yours. I wish i could help you, but it seems and
fells to me that you may want every answer to every question in one
ready-made plate. Having said that, I really really wish and hope i am
so dead wrong.

Also, seeking confirmation to our findings will not help as much as
proving them on our own by having as much as screentime and charting
practices as possible. Believe me, 2017 RTM has already structured its
materials way, way too organised compared to previous years (you can ask
 pre-2016 members, I'm so certain they'll agree), but nothing can
replace hardwork and patience after all and this is worth repeating in
our head. Just in my opinion, most of the new members here are learning
way too fast and too well that i'm a bit envy I mean it in a big compliment too

And IF has been very, very, VERY accommodating.

So, please, my only suggestion is read as much and as detailed as you
can, also analyse as thoroughly as you can. So far, for me, all, i mean
ALL, the answers on "How To Read The Market" are in this website
already. Just because we haven't found it, doesn't mean it's not there.
 Salivan's journal is one great, great journal to explore, there are so
many amazing puzzles he left there for us to find. We just need to stay
patient while have childlike curiosity & humility.

I wish you all the best of luck, and i know most members here are just
like you, possessing a great enthusiasm to beat the hell out of the
market.

text:
Hello Master Staurum, I respect your achievement, you're a Master
Trader now. You have figured everything out. I have read a few of your
posts in response to my confusion. I hope I am wrong, I think you really
 enjoy watching us suffering and enduring the pain of trying to sort out

Seriously, you are a nice guy, I have seen how generous you were in
helping people around. You took a lot of effort, in the long posts that
you wrote, telling me that my understanding of the rules is wrong (but I
 hope you would tell me why I was wrong). You have repeatedly said that
 I shouldn't expect spoon-feeding, that I should go study more charts
and figure things out myself. Your message is well-received loud and
clear. I don't blame you man, because you have absolutely no obligation
 to share of your hard earned knowledge. Plus every trader trades
differently, because we are all different human beings. I thank you for
 your encouragement. I understand that RTM is not a place where one
expects everything to be presented on a silver-platter. I actually never
 expect that. I just do not think asking questions == asking for silver
platter, especially the questions that I asked, nobody seemed to have
answers to them. When I read Hoeschec's journal, I could imagine the
ordeals he went through.

But it's all good, human are born with a brain to create, to discover,
to innovate. I love looking at candlesticks, I don't care how much money
 I am making in Forex, I have hit my 3 months target in two weeks since
 I started trading QM on LTF (THANK YOU RTM!!). If money is what I am
after, I would have stopped posting here, because I can make money even
without doing Forex. I am a Mathematician and an Engineer by background,
 hence my tendency is to get everything right. And I shouldn't apologize
 for being too precise. When something is not said, I have to assume
that it's not there. My objective in learning Forex is to crack it. RTM
had showed me the way - even though it's not a path that is nicely paved
 and luxuriously decorated, I will, eventually, figure things out to
complete the missing pieces, I have a different philosophy in life, when
 I know something, I will share.

Thank you very much and I wish you the best.

AK

GBPUSD

I wasn't ready to trade today, I was out drinking with friends, then my
phone rang, a friend called, asking me to look at GBPUSD. I looked at
the chart through my small cellphone, I saw something that's too good to
 miss. Basically, it's a QM structure, but what makes it even more
attractive is a swing low that's perfect for a FO and stop run move by
the ITs.

The trade was triggered, and TP (~8R) was hit some 40 mins later.
Master IF was right! Just learn QM, and do it well, it's all you need,
to be consistently profitable.

To all fellow traders, très bon weekend à tous !
